text:
Jordan Staal spent last June lifting the Stanley Cup and the Conn Smythe Trophy. This fall has been quieter. The 38-year-old Hurricanes captain missed more than a month after Oct. 10, returned for the Global Series game against Seattle in Helsinki on Nov. 14, and has yet to record a point in eight games.

Some of it is chance quality, some of it luck. Our numbers have the chances with him on the ice thinning out (5.4 on-ice expected goals, the quality of chances, against 6.2 usual), and his own 1.5 expected goals haven't produced a goal. Carolina's shot attempts are fine with him out there (65%), but chance quality is only even (50.7%), well behind what the team does without him.

Last season says patience. Evolving-Hockey had him better than his goals, with 1.9 expected wins against 0.7 actual, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of plenty of passes across the slot. Eight games after a long layoff is a small sample. Watch whether the chances come back with his legs.
headline: Jordan Staal is still looking for his first point
